So this line has been both looked through and punished within twelve months; the band is deliberately wide.
evidence.why_not_priced: Adjusted EPS is the denominator of the dividend policy ('at least 75% of adjusted earnings per share') and of the 14.1x forward P/E the screens carry, and it is the only headline Fonix has never pre-announced. FY25 adjusted EPS was 11.3p (FY24 10.8p, +4.6%) and the house broker's FY26 number is 11.5p — +1.8% against adjusted EBITDA up 11.0%. If that gap were in the price you would not see a stock screened on a forward P/E and a 5.63% forecast yield with a 293p consensus target against a 171p close; you would see the target cut. With one house broker publishing (the company's own AIM Rule 26 page lists Cavendish as the only analyst), there is no second estimate to arbitrage the gap.

evidence.text: Fonix's ability to buy back stock is structurally capped by Rule 9 of the Takeover Code and almost nobody outside the RNS knows it: the concert party holds 33.05% of the share capital, so the company 'has historically been restricted in its ability to conduct share buyback programmes', and the GBP 2.0m 'buyback' every aggregator reported as completed was in fact a SINGLE purchase of exactly 1,250,000 shares (1.25% of capital) at a fixed 159p, only possible because Richard Thompson, through Starnevesse Limited, signed an irrevocable undertaking to sell alongside so the concert party's interest did not increase — his holding fell 7.362603% to 6.149129% in the matching TR-1.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Capital return is the line that moves this stock most. The single largest observed reaction in the baseline's history is 2025-01-23, +5.83%, headlined 'Trading Update and Special Dividend Declaration' — the trading update alone a year later (2026-01-22, no special) moved +5.33%, and 2024-01-24 'Trading Update' moved +9.30%, so the specials are not the whole of it, but this is demonstrably a shareholder-return-owned register. FY26 broke the pattern: no special dividend was declared in January 2026 for the first time, and a GBP 2.0m structured buyback in May replaced it — on 22 May 2026 the shares closed at 159p, the buyback price, and did not re-rate.
evidence.why_not_priced: The structure is only in the RNS PDF. TipRanks describes it as 'completed a GBP 2.0 million share buyback, reflecting strong cash generation and the board's confidence' (https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/fonix-lifts-profits-and-steps-up-european-push-as-mobile-payments-pipeline-grows) and Kalkine as a 'GBP 2.0 million programme' — neither mentions Rule 9, the 33.05% concert party or the matching irrevocable, and the issuer's own 23 July summary of it says only 'the Group also completed a GBP 2.0m on-market share buyback, underlining the Board's confidence'. So the read available to anyone who did not open the May RNS is 'this company now runs buybacks', when the true read is 'this company can only run a buyback when a named 6.1% holder agrees to sell into it'. If the market knew, the finals' capital-return line would not carry an open-ended-buyback option in the price at all. The direction is modestly negative because it removes an upside scenario rather than creating a downside one: the promised increase in the FINAL DIVIDEND is the one return that needs nobody's permission, and it is contractually ~75-78% of an adjusted EPS that grew ~2% in H1.
evidence.independence: The matching TR-1, a different document filed the same day by a different party: Starnevesse Limited, threshold crossed 22-May-2026, resulting 6.149129% / 6,003,005 shares against a previous notification of 7.362603% — https://www.fonix.com/?jet_download=3d9ff2739423f0be1229997702baa61f25dca27a. evidence.text: On 9 September 2026 M+C Saatchi announced that the Parc-backed management buyout of its Australia and New Zealand advertising agency had failed due diligence and that the business will instead CEASE OPERATIONS before the end of 2026, with the entire ANZ leadership team and all staff departing and Woolworths finishing in November. There is no RNS on the subject -- not for the 22 July MBO agreement and not for the 9 September collapse and closure -- and no UK financial outlet has covered it. The 22 September interim statement is the first regulated document in which the UK market can see it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Australia has been the line that moves this stock. The 18 Sep 2025 interims, which carried the Australian restructure and the closure of the Bohemia media unit, produced -12.24% -- by far the largest of the 13 observed reactions (median |move| 1.98%). The 24 Nov 2025 trading update, which downgraded the FY25 decline to 7%, produced -5.16%. But the 20 Apr 2026 FY results, which disclosed FY25 separately-disclosed items of GBP9.1m 'largely restructuring costs in Australia' alongside the language 'simplify the businesses ... unlock the intrinsic value', produced +3.91%. So this line has moved the stock hard in both directions, and the sign has tracked whether Australia was presented as a continuing problem or as a problem being removed. This time it is being removed entirely.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Investegate RNS record for M&C Saatchi from 1 July 2026 to 21 September 2026 contains nothing but Transaction in Own Shares, three Holding(s) in Company and the Notice of Half Year Results -- no announcement of the MBO, none of its collapse, none of the closure. Every outlet carrying it is Australian trade press (Campaign Brief, Campaign Brief NZ, Campaign Brief Asia, Mumbrella, Mediaweek, B&T, Mi3). Sharecast covered this issuer's March 2026 CEO change, so it follows the name, and it did not carry this. If the market had priced the closure of an entire country's advertising operations announced with no consideration and all staff departing, the stock would not be sitting at 147p on 21 September, within 2% of its 52-week high of 150p and up 29% from its April low of 113.5p; nor would a break-up activist have crossed 9% on 18 September. What the tape shows instead is a 149p-to-142p drift from 8 to 11 September fully given back by 18 September on ordinary volume -- consistent with a handful of holders reading the Australian trade press, not with the information being in the price. Size: APAC was 18% of FY25 like-for-like group net revenue (GBP204.7m) and fell 22.3%, 'predominantly Australia'; Australia alone fell 31.9% and accounts for the whole gap between the -3.1% group decline ex-Australia and the -7.3% including it. Removing it structurally lifts continuing-group organic growth by roughly 3-4pp and lifts margin; against that sit closure costs on top of FY25's GBP9.1m of separately-disclosed items (largely Australian restructuring), cash out rather than in, and an FY27 consensus of GBP221.8m / +3.6% organic that has to come down on the revenue line. That two-sidedness is why the band spans -4.5 to +5.5 and the point estimate is only +1.2. Net of the rest of the company: this rests on one region, and it requires H1 net revenue and margin to be at least in line, which the 11 June AGM update (Jan-Apr, LFL net revenue in line and supportive of the full year outlook) and an easy cost comparative support -- H1 2025 LFL operating margin was 9.9% after first-half-weighted investment in senior talent that has since annualised, and group central costs fell from GBP12.4m to GBP6.1m.
evidence.independence: Independently reported the same day by Mumbrella ('M&C Saatchi is preparing to exit Australia, ending a 30-year run'; 'the Australian business will be folded by November'; 'Woolworths will be the last remaining client ... with its contract ending in November') at https://mumbrella.com.au/mc-saatchi-australia-set-to-close-936541 , and by Campaign Brief Asia at https://campaignbriefasia.com/2026/09/09/mc-saatchi-australia-new-zealand-advertising-agency-management-buyout-no-longer-proceeding/ . evidence.text: The 50% Section 338 tariff on Canadian imports that took DOO from C$93.82 to C$83.67 between 21 and 26 August explicitly does not apply to goods already subject to Section 232 duties - and BRP's snowmobiles and 'the majority of ORV models' have been Section 232 derivative articles at 25% of full value since 6 April 2026, by BRP's own disclosure.
evidence.source_date: 2026-08-22 (effective date stated in document; Section 338 took effect 12:01am ET 22 Aug 2026)
evidence.why_not_priced: If the market had worked through the non-stacking carve-out, DOO would not have tracked Magna one-for-one on 24 August (DOO -5.94%, Magna -6.56%) when Magna IS the Section 232 auto/parts complex and BRP is Mexico-origin recreational vehicles already inside Section 232. And the gap would have closed over the following six sessions as trade counsel published the annex analyses - instead DOO closed 2 Sep at 85.90, still 8.4% below the 21 Aug close. A targeted search for any note, wire item or trade-press piece connecting BRP to the Section 232 exclusion returned nothing: BRP has issued no release since 18 August and its next scheduled communication is tomorrow's 09:00 EDT call. Coverage that had priced this would read 'BRP largely exempt from Section 338'; no such sentence exists.
evidence.independence: Holland & Knight, a separate firm, states the same exclusion independently and adds that the proclamation named for 'motor vehicles' does not in fact reach vehicles because they are already under Section 232 (https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/07/50-percent-opening-bid-canadian-imports-subject-to-section-338-tariffs). Separately, the Globe and Mail documents that ~75% of BRP units are produced across four Mexican facilities in Juarez and Queretaro with 60% of output sold in the US, so the Canada-origin share of US-bound volume is a minority regardless of the carve-out (https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-us-tariffs-turn-ski-doo-maker-brps-mexico-production-hub-into-a/, 2025-02-03).

Every BRP note is about the CAD 500-550m Section 232 number; none is about the refundable pre-February tariff base.

evidence.why_not_priced: Nobody cross-reads NOAA NCEI into a vertical-SaaS name, and the coverage proves it: the 4-Sep-2026 preview of this print says the two metrics that will define the quarter are subscription revenue growth and margin progress, and treats trades demand only as a qualitative risk ('when demand in those trades cools, there is no other segment to absorb the impact'). If this were priced, the >110% NDR line would be treated as de-risked rather than as the swing factor, and the 25-delta skew would not be paying for downside.

evidence.text: DBI's Q1 10-Q discloses it sold the rights to its IEEPA tariff claims to an unnamed Investor before the 20 Feb 2026 Supreme Court ruling and expects to recognise approximately $20.0m to income (claims value less the Investor's portion, net of proceeds already received) for tariff recoveries, with no receivable booked as of 2 May 2026 because it applied the gain-contingency model — $20.0m is ~$0.36/share pre-tax on 55.9m diluted shares and ~7% of the $290m market cap, and none of it is in the FY26 $0.28-$0.38 EPS guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: Gain-contingency accounting means the number appears nowhere in the Q1 press release, nowhere in the reaffirmed FY guide, and nowhere in Q1 reported or adjusted EPS — it exists only in the Commitments & Contingencies note of a 10-Q for a company with two remaining sell-side analysts (UBS Neutral, Telsey Market Perform). If it were priced, the stock would not be -16.75% over twenty sessions into a print that can mechanically deliver ~7% of market cap in cash, and previews would frame the quarter around a tariff recovery instead of quoting a garbled adjusted-EPS consensus that aggregators variously print as $0.25, $0.22 and -$0.06. The claim-sale-to-an-Investor structure is also unique to DBI among footwear names and is not something a screen surfaces.
evidence.independence: Caleres, a footwear importer whose Q2 ended 2 Aug 2026 (one day after DBI's 1 Aug quarter end), reported on 2026-09-09 that it recognised $55.6m of IEEPA tariff recoveries in cost of goods sold, which establishes that CBP CAPE payouts to footwear importers actually landed inside this exact fiscal window rather than slipping to Q3: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CAL/caleres-reports-second-quarter-2026-cbjhhvcqm4mz.html . evidence.independence: Two different sources point the same way from different directions: NOAA/NCEI's August and summer 2026 temperature record (https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/news/national-climate-202608) is the macro series, and ORLY's own management commentary is the direct-counterparty statement of the transmission mechanism. They share no document. The honest limit, and it is the reason this is 1.3 and not 3: the July leg is stated by a counterparty, the August leg is my inference from a weather series, and reasoning from weather is explicitly on the list of what has NOT paid in this stage's resolved days.

evidence.text: AZO's LIFO reserve has been built entirely by tariff inflation - the 10-Q states 'Due to price changes on the Company's merchandise purchases, primarily due to inflation driven by tariffs, the Company's LIFO credit reserve balance was $260.0 million at May 9, 2026, and $83.0 million at August 30, 2025' - and Q4 FY26 carries the easiest LIFO comp of the year (guided ~$30m charge, 45bp, against an actual $80m charge / 128bp in Q4 FY25), with upside to a credit if supplier pass-back of IEEPA refunds lowers replacement cost in the May-August window, which is the exact line the stock has been sold on for three consecutive quarters.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin with LIFO as the swing factor is the stated cause of the last three selloffs: Q3 FY26 gross margin 52.2%, -57bp, with a 77bp LIFO charge cited as the primary driver, and the stock fell 8.99%; Q4 FY25 gross margin 51.5%, -98bp on a 128bp LIFO impact, and EPS fell 5.6% reported against +8.7% ex-LIFO. The market has punished this line hard when it went the wrong way; it has never been tested with it going the right way on this name, which is why the band is wide and the point estimate is small.
evidence.why_not_priced: Only the delta to the guide is unpriced and I say so: the $30m Q4 charge was guided on the 2026-05-26 call, so the +83bp YoY improvement is inside what the company already told the market to expect and is a reported-quarter item. What is not in any preview I could find is that the reserve is now $260m built from tariff inflation that the Supreme Court voided on 2026-02-20, and that peer retailers are already booking the reversal - AAP took $26m of tariff refunds worth 130bp of gross margin in its July quarter, Target applied $685m of $730m of refunds to reduce COGS, and ORLY says it is negotiating supplier sharing of refunds. If the market had priced a possible LIFO credit rather than the guided charge, the sell-side gross-margin cuts into this print would not be running the other way.
evidence.independence: Independent of finding 1 - different document (the 10-Q, not a peer transcript) and a different P&L line (gross margin, not comp). Corroboration from a different source: https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/oreilly-automotive-suppliers-sharing-tariff-refund-benefits/827111/ on supplier pass-back, and AAP's own $26m / 130bp refund benefit in the quarter ending mid-July. The counterweight I have already netted into the 0.6: the upside-to-guide leg rests on other retailers' cost behaviour, not on an AZO document, and AZO itself reports and is modelled on ex-LIFO EPS, so the market has a habit of looking through this line in both directions.

evidence.text: The FY2026 10-K, due roughly late October 2026, is where the full-year LIFO reserve roll-forward and any IEEPA tariff refund or gain-contingency disclosure will appear in primary form; CBP's CAPE liquidation process was still running at ~$128.7bn of accepted refunds as of 2026-07-31, so supplier pass-back to AZO continues to accrue after this print.

A direct IEEPA tariff refund receivable or gain contingency in AZO's own filings - the Q3 FY26 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/866787/000110465926073525/azo-20260509x10q.htm) carries no IEEPA, refund, customs or gain-contingency language at all, and AZO's model is supplier-as-importer-of-record like ORLY's, so there is no AAP-style direct refund line to find here

FX as an edge: I computed it and it is not differentiated. FRED DEXMXUS monthly averages (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=DEXMXUS) give USD/MXN ~17.30 across May-Aug 2026 against ~18.97 across May-Aug 2025, a ~9.7% YoY peso tailwind - but that is SMALLER than the ~15% YoY move in the Q3 window that produced the $74m sales / $0.83 EPS benefit, so naively scaling Q3's FX benefit over 16 weeks overstates Q4 by roughly $0.40. Decelerating tailwind, routinely modelled, no edge

A buyback slowdown: none detectable. $586.3m / 164k shares at $3,582 in Q3, $800m remaining, then a further $1.5bn authorised 2026-06-16 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000866787/000117184326004150/exh_991.htm) and $850m of 4.950% notes due 2031 completed 2026-07-14 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000866787/000110465926083528/tm2620403d1_8k.htm). The financing question answered: the money terms out commercial paper and funds repurchase capacity, corroborated by the incremental authorisation - it is not distress and it is not a finding
A quiet 8-K, management change or unusual filing in the run-in - AZO's only 8-Ks since June 2026 are the buyback authorisation and the two notes-offering filings
A squeeze setup - 2.67% of float short and 1.94 days to cover leaves no mechanism in either direction

Gasoline prices as a positive - they are a negative and they cut against me: US averages of roughly $4.05 (June), $3.93 (July) and $4.06-4.19 (August) 2026, higher YoY in every state (https://www.lendingtree.com/credit-cards/study/us-gas-prices/), which supports AAP's 'tighter household budgets' DIY read rather than mine, and I have netted it into the sizes rather than filing it twice

first_hunter_context.positioning_check: 11.65m shares short, 3.40% of float, 2.91% of shares out, 6.40 days to cover, up from 10.36m the prior month (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ctas/statistics/, read 2026-09-22). The sweep read the build as bearish; the arithmetic says it is almost entirely merger-arb hedge and carries no fundamental signal. UniFirst has 18.08m shares out and 13.05m of float (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/unf/statistics/, 2026-09-22) against an exchange ratio of 0.7720 CTAS per UNF share, so a full arb hedge is 10.1m CTAS shares on the float alone and 14.0m on all shares out — the 11.65m short sits inside that envelope. UNF trades $265.42 against deal value of $155 cash + 0.7720 x $196.50 = $306.70, a 15.6% gross spread, consistent with the ~70% approval odds Bernstein cites. Consequences: there is no squeeze mechanism here (the short is delta-hedged by a long UNF that moves 0.772-for-1 with CTAS, so a beat does not force covering), and equally no forced selling. The one asymmetry is that bad deal news causes arbs to BUY CTAS back, which damps deal-driven downside — but I cannot sign the deal news, so that is variance, not a size. Baseline skew is -1.01 vol points, i.e. calls bid over puts, a mild UPSIDE lean; put/call OI ratio of 1.65 sits on only 1,637 total contracts with a 19.4%-of-mid ATM spread, so the 4.41% implied move is a thin-chain artefact as much as a forecast (20-day realised vol is 12.1% annualised and the name's median reaction is 3.69%).

evidence.text: The FTC second request of 2026-06-11 is not close to resolved: Cintas is due to complete its compliance response between September and November 2026, the FTC has issued expansive civil investigative demands to third-party industry participants, and market-implied approval odds have fallen from ~85% on 25 Aug to ~70%, with Bernstein now expecting an early-2027 close against management's stated 'second half of calendar 2026'. Management will almost certainly have to address the timing on the 10:00 ET call, but the regulatory event itself cannot land by the 2026-09-23 close.

The 8-K of 2026-06-12 confirms the Second Request extends the HSR waiting period until 30 days after both parties substantially comply — a clock that by construction runs past the exit window, and whose outcome (clearance, divestiture, or a $350m reverse termination fee to UniFirst if blocked on antitrust grounds) is the single largest unpriced binary on this equity.

Extra FY2027 workday: I counted it independently (Q1 FY2027 = 65 workdays vs 64 in Q1 FY2026 after the observed 3 July holiday, a +1.56pp revenue tailwind concentrated in this quarter against the +0.40pp full-year figure). Management stated exactly this on the 2026-07-15 call — 'The first quarter of fiscal year 27 has 1 extra day... The second quarter has the same number of workdays. The third quarter has 1 less workday. And then the fourth quarter has 1 more workday' (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/22/cintas-ctas-q4-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). A number management reads out on a transcript is not unpriced.

Fuel cost as a gross-margin surprise — the one lead I thought I had, and it falsified. Diesel looked dramatic (EIA monthly: Jun-Aug 2026 avg $5.147 vs $3.707 a year earlier, +38.8%, and DOWN from $5.341 in Mar-May 2026), which would have implied an easing YoY comp on the record 51.0% gross margin. But Cintas runs a gasoline van fleet, and on the correct series the comp barely moves: gasoline Jun-Aug 2026 $4.013 vs $3.136, +27.9%, against Mar-May 2026 $4.073 vs $3.139, +29.8% (https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=pet&s=emm_epmr_pte_nus_dpg&f=m). Applying management's own stated elasticity — fuel is ~100bp of revenue and a 20% fuel price move is ~20bp of margin — the YoY fuel headwind eases by roughly 2bp quarter-on-quarter, i.e. nothing. Dropped rather than filed.

Cintas M&A in the quarter: no bolt-on acquisition 8-K or press release between 2026-07-15 and today, so no inorganic revenue the street has not modelled. The only EDGAR events since the print are a 2026-08-03 8-K promoting Jim Rozakis to President & COO, a 2026-08-27 8-K on a director not standing for re-election, the 2026-09-15 DEF 14A/ARS, and Form 4 clusters on 2026-08-12 and 2026-09-17 — all routine for a company whose executives sell continuously under plan.

Competitor read-through: Vestis (the nearest pure-play) reported its quarter ended 2026-07-03 on 2026-08-11 with revenue -1.8% and pounds processed -4.5%, and left its FY2026 revenue growth outlook unchanged at (2.0)% to flat (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001967649/000162828026055485/vstsq3fy26earningsrelease-.htm). Discarded: Vestis has been losing share to Cintas for two years, so its volume decline is as likely to be a Cintas tailwind as an industry signal, and it is exactly the narrow-proxy trap — it also overlaps only one of Cintas's three months.
UniFirst as a direct counterparty on the same calendar quarter: UNF's fiscal Q4 ends late August and is reported in October, so nothing from the acquiree covers Jun-Aug 2026 ahead of this print.

Cintas hiring as a wearer-growth proxy: careers.cintas.com currently shows 244 route service and 119 service sales openings, but no archived time series exists to compare against, so the level carries no information.

Employment-sensitivity as a transmission channel: no company or direct-counterparty statement connects Jun-Aug small-business payrolls to Cintas wearer counts for this quarter, and Cintas's organic growth has accelerated (7.8% in Q1 FY26 to 8.4% in Q4 FY26) through a soft employment backdrop on price and cross-sell. Left as a hypothesis, not a finding.

Financing: no debt issuance, 424B, FWP or shelf takedown since the deal was signed. The $2.8bn cash leg is covered by committed bridge financing from Morgan Stanley, KeyBank and Wells Fargo arranged in March, and the FY2027 guide's ~$105m interest expense assumption explicitly excludes UniFirst, so there is no pre-funding event to sign either way.
Proxy/governance: PRE 14A 2026-08-28 and DEF 14A 2026-09-15 carry nothing unusual — no share authorisation increase is needed for the ~14m shares of stock consideration against 400.7m outstanding.
